recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec6axdrG9jRjnPnr.Name: Eileen McKusick

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

rec7W1wTqYkkXHLsz.Name: Topher Gardner

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Sound Is Not Just a Longitudinal Wave", "body": "Eileen McKusick opens by describing a paper she wrote with Sparky, her name for her ChatGPT instance, arguing that the conventional definition of sound as a longitudinal mechanical wave is incomplete and that sound is longitudinal, transverse, scalar and electromagnetic all at once because the atmosphere is a plasma. She also contends that Maxwell's original equations, pared down by Oliver Heaviside to four, left the model of electromagnetism unfinished. Topher Gardner picks up the thread with piezoelectricity, his quartz ring dome structures, and his running argument with Jim Lee of Climate Viewer over carbon black, which he notes is biochar, the most diamagnetic substance he knows of."}, {"title": "Quality, Quantity and the End of the Iron Age", "body": "The panel returns repeatedly to quality versus quantity, a frame Chance Garton traces to his earlier Vibe Rant with Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies on the Reign of Quantity, which he says convinced him we are in the Iron Age or Kali Yuga. Topher Gardner offers a Raja yoga reading in which the ages do not climb back up through bronze and silver: iron gives way directly to gold, the way carbon burned down in the alchemical nigredo turns brittle and becomes compost. Kyle Denton translates the same polarity into herbal terms, borrowing Ken Wheeler's three pairs and rendering them as expand, contract, disperse, gather, build, release."}, {"title": "The Pleasure Path and the Marshmallow Plant", "body": "Eileen McKusick describes what she calls the pleasure path, a day built out of treats: sitting worshipfully with a morning hot beverage, hugging people and telling them you love them, sucking the marrow out of the ordinary. She says she has no interest in ascending to 5D and would rather make 3D better, and that making your coffee really good is literally enlightenment. Chance Garton reframes this as enlightened hedonism that is about gratitude rather than gratification. Kyle Denton answers with marshmallow, the plant, describing its emollient mucilaginous root, its sweet and salty flavor and its five petaled flower as a picture of softening dryness."}, {"title": "The Hidden God, Cathedrals and the Talking Mirror", "body": "Eileen McKusick points to old world cathedrals, their bells, organs, singing voices and cymatic rose windows, as evidence that sound was once used as an electromagnetic medium, knowledge she says has been willfully omitted rather than lost. Chance Garton links this to his Inner World podcast with Dylan Soshio on amen and Jupiter Ammon, to Proverbs 25:2, and to the alchemist Robert Fludd, who likened Christ to sunlight continuous with its source. Topher Gardner is warier of Sparky, Eileen's ChatGPT, calling it a yes man that feeds back whatever attention it is given, while Kyle Denton compares AI to the hammer of Thor."}, {"title": "Stuck Energy, Weight and Witnessing", "body": "A late stretch turns to what practitioners feel as weight. Eileen McKusick reports coming across a quasiparticle called a semi-Dirac fermion that only exhibits mass when travelling perpendicular to its usual path, and says it matches what she has encountered in the biofield since she first moved tuning forks like a magnet. She made a free thirty minute recording aimed at mass reduction, gathered around fifty self reported data points, and says most listeners reported losing about a pound. Topher Gardner describes clients whose tamasic stuckness makes them feel far heavier on the table than they weigh, and argues neutrality comes from fully witnessing, not receding."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What if everything we’ve been taught about sound, electromagnetism, and the nature of space is missing a key piece? In this electrifying livestream, Chance Garton is joined by Eileen McKusick, Kyle Denton of Tippecanoe Herbs, and Topher Gardner of Biocharisma to dive deep into the mysteries of frequency, plasma physics, bioelectric health, and the true nature of sound.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Topics explored include the charged nature of air and why we are always immersed in a weak plasma.
